articles.title: Manufacturers lean into automation as skilled hiring remains difficult across the sector
articles.excerpt: Plant managers say robotics investment is now as much about labour shortages as it is about efficiency.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: A robotic arm on an assembly line | EP
content: Manufacturers across the sector are accelerating investment in automation, with plant managers increasingly citing labour shortages rather than pure efficiency as the driving factor.
Industry surveys show vacancies for skilled technical roles have remained elevated for over a year despite wage increases in several regions.
Trade groups are calling for expanded vocational training programmes to close the gap over the medium term.

articles.title: Regional industrial parks report near-full occupancy for the first time in a decade
articles.excerpt: Developers say reshoring and nearshoring demand has filled space that sat vacant for years.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: Warehouses at a regional industrial park | EP
content: Several regional industrial parks are reporting occupancy rates above 90 percent, a level not seen in more than a decade, according to commercial property data.
Developers attribute the shift to a wave of reshoring and nearshoring activity, as manufacturers seek to shorten supply chains after years of global disruption.
Local authorities in some regions have begun approving new park developments to meet demand that existing sites can no longer absorb.

articles.title: The component shortage that hit manufacturers for years is finally easing
articles.excerpt: Lead times for key electronic and mechanical parts have returned to pre-2021 levels, industry data shows.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: Electronic components on a production line | EP
content: Lead times for a range of electronic and mechanical components have returned to pre-2021 levels, according to data tracked by several industry associations.
The easing comes after years of disruption that forced manufacturers to hold larger inventories and, in some cases, redesign products around whatever parts were available.
Some firms say they are now reassessing those inventory buffers, though others plan to keep a portion in place as insurance against future shocks.

articles.title: Steelmakers commit to a new round of low-carbon plant upgrades
articles.excerpt: The investments aim to cut emissions ahead of tightening EU carbon border rules.
articles.author: carlos-cozar
articles.imageCaption: A steel plant undergoing upgrade works | EP
content: Several major steelmakers have committed to a new round of investment in low-carbon production technology, aiming to cut emissions ahead of tightening EU carbon border rules.
The upgrades include electric arc furnace conversions and pilot projects using hydrogen in place of coking coal at select plants.
Industry groups say the transition will require continued public support given the scale of capital involved, even as first movers report early efficiency gains.

articles.title: Vocational training enrolment climbs as industry pushes to close the skills gap
articles.excerpt: New dual-training schemes pairing classroom study with paid factory placements are drawing record applicants.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: Trainees working on machinery in a vocational workshop | EP
content: Enrolment in vocational training programmes tied to manufacturing has climbed sharply this year, as industry groups push new schemes to close a persistent skills gap.
The most successful programmes pair classroom instruction with paid placements on factory floors, an approach that organisers say improves completion rates over purely academic courses.
Employers involved in the schemes say early graduates have been absorbed into permanent roles faster than through traditional hiring channels.
